narration: The first peg slides free with a glassy chirp. The grate lifts a finger’s width and exhales hard enough to flatten the candle flame; warm salt air—not rain-cold wind—spills around your boots. William looks from the opening to the families running downhill. “I’ll turn them here,” he says. “If this is a trap, keep it alive until I return.” He sprints into the rain, striking your three-note rhythm on his message tube. The child stays, counting the two remaining pegs aloud while your candle marks the draft.
